title: A technique to enhance stability and esthetics of an interim obturator
html: The rehabilitation of a hemimaxillectomy defect is more challenging than providing a conventional prosthesis. Maxillary obturators can be fabricated using various techniques. For this patient, a hollow obturator prosthesis was constructed by adding a bow and clasp along with an acrylic resin pad to provide additional support. The bow was made from 23-gauge stainless steel wrought wire and the clasp from 21-gauge. To enhance the esthetics, the interdental papilla was carved by eliminating the clasp arm from the primary anterior abutment.
